docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to complexipy are documented here, newest first. Each release section links to its GitHub release notes for the full details.

Migration

This release applies more of the cognitive complexity paper's rules, so scores change. On the django source tree, 1,946 of 30,813 functions change score: 1,481 go down and 465 go up, and the total of all files drops by 7%. Re-run complexipy after upgrading and review your thresholds and snapshots. Scripts that read --plain output, or warnings on stdout, also need a change. See the migration guide for upgrade guidance.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• --diff, --diff-only, and --staged list, below the diff table, each function that an ignore comment hides now but did not hide at the reference, as path:line function score, the score taken with the comment disregarded. The list never changes the exit code, and --quiet hides it (#327).
  • Each JSON entry carries line_start, line_end, and line_complexities: the lines that add to the score, one entry per line in line order, whose complexity values sum to the function's complexity. Two functions with one name in one file are now told apart by their lines. CSV, GitLab, and SARIF output do not change (#325).
  • --output - writes the report to stdout when exactly one --output-format is selected, so complexipy . --output-format json --output - | jq . works. stdout then holds only the report: the console output is suppressed as with --quiet, and warnings and errors go to stderr. The exit code is the same as with a file. With two or more formats, --output - fails before the analysis runs (#324).
  • The language server answers textDocument/codeAction with one code action per refactoring suggestion of each function over the threshold in the requested range. A suggestion --fix would apply is a quick fix that rewrites the buffer in one edit built by the same fix engine; any other suggestion is a disabled refactor action with its help text as the reason, and never edits. Each title states the reduction, or says it is not measured. The threshold diagnostic now links to its documentation through codeDescription (#254).
  • --select, --ignore, and the select and ignore configuration keys accept a rule group: complexity or readability. A group stands for every refactoring rule of that category, and mixes with rule ids, as in --select complexity,C007. A group name prints no unknown-rule warning (#205).
  • The language server publishes diagnostics for files that are not open when [lsp] workspace-diagnostics = true. It scans each workspace folder with the same file discovery and exclusion as complexipy, and refreshes a file when it is closed or changes on disk. The setting is off by default. A client that supports dynamic file watching now also reports .py changes to the server, which ignores them while the setting is off (#256).
  • --explain <rule> prints a refactoring rule's id, name, category, applicability, description, and documentation link, and exits without running an analysis. An unknown rule id exits with an error that lists the valid ids (#207).
  • --fix applies C005 (extract predicate). It inserts the helper above the module-level def or class that holds the function and rewrites the condition into a call. It does so only when every name the condition reads is sure to be bound; other conditions keep the snippet for hand application. C005 reduction is measured when the fix applies. CodeSuggestion gains insertions, a list of the new CodeInsertion type, and the JSON output gains the insertions key (#263).
  • --force-exclude, also force-exclude = true in the configuration, applies exclude patterns to files passed explicitly as arguments. Without it, an explicit file is analyzed as before. Pass it under pre-commit, which names each changed file, so the configured exclude applies there (#293).
  • The configuration schema is in the SchemaStore catalog, so a TOML language server such as Taplo completes and validates complexipy.toml, .complexipy.toml, and [tool.complexipy] in pyproject.toml with no #:schema line (#270).

docs.title: Changed (scoring)
docs.text:
• Comprehension for and if clauses add nothing and no longer raise the nesting level, since a comprehension is shorthand for a loop. else on for, while, and try adds +1 with no nesting increment, and its body raises the nesting level, like else after if: the paper's hybrid increment. Mixed boolean operators are read left to right, so a or b and c or d scores 3 instead of 2. Scores drop for code with comprehensions and rise for loop and try else. Some mixed conditions score higher and some lower: (a or (b and c)) and d goes from 3 to 2 (#342, #351).
  • Each function in a recursion cycle adds +1: indirect cycles (a calls b, b calls a), methods that call self.m() or cls.m(), and nested functions, whose +1 goes to the enclosing function, as the paper prescribes. Calls resolve within one file, by the rules in Understanding Complexity Scores. A method that calls a bare name equal to its own, such as def get(self): return get(x), no longer scores as recursive (#340).
  • A call through the class name, such as K.s() in a static method of K, now counts toward a recursion cycle when K names exactly one class of the file and no other binding of K can replace it (#354, #363).
  • A bare-name call no longer counts as recursion when another binding hides the function, such as a parameter, an assignment, or an import, so def f(f): return f() scores 0. When a scope binds the name both by def and another way, the call counts only if the other binding always runs first: f = 1 before def f keeps the +1, and f = wrap(f) after it removes it (#361).
  • A recursive call inside a lambda, or in the decorators, default arguments, bases, or class body of a definition nested in a function, now counts for the enclosing function. Lambda parameters, comprehension variables, and type parameters hide outer names, so lambda f: f() inside f is not recursive (#349).
  • A nested function raises the nesting level of its body wherever it sits, under if, for, while, with, try, match, or in a class, as the paper prescribes. Before, only a def placed directly in a function body did. A class body inside a function is now scored in full, and a class does not raise the nesting level itself. With --check-script, the body of a module-level class counts toward <module>; method bodies do not (#339).
  • The Python decorator exception applies only when a function returns its nested function, by name or as a direct argument of a call such as functools.wraps(f)(inner), so return inner() no longer drops the nesting increment. A leading docstring no longer stops the exception, and the expressions in the return now count (#341, #353).
  • A conditional expression, a boolean operator sequence, or a comprehension in a case guard now counts, at the nesting level of the match. The guard itself adds nothing, unlike the +1 of an elif. A complex guard can get a C005 plan with help text (#338, #352).
  • The decorators and defaults of a module-level def, the decorators, bases, and keywords of a module-level class, and the headers of their direct methods now count toward module scope: the <module> entry with --check-script, and the file total without it. This also holds for an ignored function. Function scores do not change (#338).
  • A conditional expression, a boolean operator sequence, or a comprehension now counts in more statement parts: assignment, augmented assignment, annotated assignment, del, for, and with ... as targets, the match subject, and except types. The decorators and defaults of a nested def, and the decorators, bases, and keywords of a nested class, count toward the enclosing function at the nesting level of the definition. Scores of functions that hold these sites go up. A complex match subject or except type can now get a C005 plan, with help text and no suggestion (#336).

docs.title: Changed (CLI and output)
docs.text:
• --plain prints each function as <path>:<line> <function> <complexity>, so editors and terminals can link to the line. With --suggest-refactors, each plan adds an indented line with its rule id, title, and reduction, for example C007 Merge 3 nested if statements (-4); a ~ marks an estimated reduction. Scripts that parse the first field of a --plain line now get :<line> after the path (#326).
  • The C005 helper no longer carries a -> bool annotation, because and and or return an operand, not a bool (#263).
  • Every CLI warning prints to stderr, and --quiet no longer hides warnings: it hides the report only. The --diff and --staged warnings moved from stdout to stderr, so they no longer mix with a report that another tool reads from a pipe (#294).

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: • The aarch64 musllinux wheel allocates with mimalloc, like the x86_64 one. On the django source tree it runs about 4 to 5 times faster (#303).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• A new AI Agent Workflows page shows how to run complexipy from coding-agent hooks (thanks to @anhaoXie in #330).
  • The home page shows what complexipy does, and the usage guide is split into focused pages (#322, #323).
  • The ruff comparison and the scores page show the scores this release computes (#348).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A conditional expression counts wherever it sits inside an expression. It used to count only as a statement's value, a positional argument, or an element of a list, tuple, set, or dict value, and counted 0 in a keyword argument, a dict key, a method chain, an attribute, a subscript, a binary operation, an await, an f-string, a called lambda, a lambda parameter default, or an operand of -, ~, not, and, or or, so f(k=a if b else c) scored 0. Boolean operator sequences and comprehensions in the same places count too, so (a or b) + 1 now scores 1. Scores rise for functions that use these forms (#334, thanks to @glictevo in #335).
  • The x86_64 musllinux wheel imports again. In 8.3.0 it failed on import with initial-exec TLS resolves to dynamic definition, because mimalloc used a thread-local storage model that musl cannot load from a Python extension (#311).

See the release notes for the full details.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• A run gated by --diff or --staged shows which functions fail it. A REGRESSED or NEW function above the threshold is listed as FAILED and marked FAILS in the diff table, which ends with a Gate: line that counts them. A function above the threshold that the gate lets through is listed as ALLOWED instead of FAILED, and --failed lists only the functions that fail the run. A snapshot run lists the functions its snapshot lets through as ALLOWED too, instead of PASSED.
  • SARIF output is diff-aware. With a diff, every result carries the baselineState of its function, new, unchanged, or updated, against the reference, and when the diff decides the exit code a complexity result's level is error for a function that fails the run, through the gate or the snapshot, and note for one the run lets through. The GitLab Code Quality report rates the same functions major and info. Fingerprints are unchanged.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• --diff and --diff-only read each file from the repository that holds it, so a run from outside the repository compares against the ref instead of reporting every function as NEW. A submodule, a repository that the repository around it tracks as a gitlink, is read at the commit the outer repository pins for it at the ref, unless the run starts inside it. A file outside any repository, a ref that names no commit in the file's repository, or a submodule without a pinned commit it has, still reports its functions as NEW, and the run now prints a warning that names the cause.
  • --diff-only alone no longer warns that --diff and --diff-only are both set.
  • --staged compares only the staged files the run selects: the path arguments, paths, and exclude apply as they do without it, so complexipy one.py --staged no longer reports the other staged files. They apply to the index, so a staged regular file is compared whatever the working tree holds at its path. A staged deletion that discovery would have selected still reports its functions as REMOVED: under a selected directory, outside hidden paths, and not matched by exclude, .gitignore, .ignore, or git's exclude file. Each file is named by the path the rest of the run reports.
  • A rename or a move no longer fails --diff or --staged when the function's body stays as it was. A file that git pairs as renamed compares with its old path when the run covers that path, and as added when it moves in from outside the selected paths; a file moved out of them reports nothing. A function above the threshold that the change adds passes only when it replaces a REMOVED function with the same body and at least its complexity, each removed function replaced once, and the compared files (modified, renamed from a covered path, deleted from a covered path, or added) do not hold more functions with that body than they did at the ref, counting the functions that ignore comments hide. Bodies count and pair only within the repository that holds each file. Bodies compare structurally, without formatting, comments, the name, the decorators, or the parameters, so a function or class rename, a move to another file, and a method that becomes a function pass, and a function that moves and changes fails. The diff table names, in a Gate column, the REMOVED function each passing one replaces. has_regressions sees no bodies, so it still fails a moved function above the threshold. A function that an ignore comment now hides is not reported as REMOVED. A deleted Python file that discovery would have selected reports its functions as REMOVED in --diff too, and a deleted symbolic link reports nothing. The snapshot gate does not pair functions: a moved or renamed function above the threshold fails it until --snapshot-create records the function again, and a snapshot rewrite drops the entries of files that no longer exist.
  • --diff reports the functions of a file that does not parse at the reference as NEW, as --staged does, instead of leaving the file out of the comparison.
  • The C002 loop guard negates its condition the way a linter expects: x in y becomes x not in y, a is b becomes a is not b, and a name or a call gets a bare not, so --fix no longer writes E713/E714 violations. Parentheses stay around and, or, other comparisons, conditional expressions, lambdas, and walrus assignments.

See the release notes for the full details.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• file_complexity() and code_complexity() take with_plans, True by default. Pass with_plans=False to skip building refactor plans when only the scores are needed.
  • The language server answers complexipy/lineComplexities with the total of every function and the increment of every line, whatever the hint settings say. The VS Code extension draws its colored badges from it (#292).
  • [lsp] diagnostic-range and [lsp] hover choose what the warning underlines and where hover answers.
  • --isolated ignores every configuration file, and --config <path> reads only the named file: its [tool.complexipy] section when the file is named pyproject.toml, and the whole file otherwise. The two flags cannot be combined. Pass either one in CI to pin the gate, so a change to the repository's configuration cannot change it.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The language server is quieter by default. The warning underlines the function name instead of the whole function, and hover answers only on the def lines, so it no longer covers the editor's own hover inside the body (#290). Set diagnostic-range = "function" or hover = "function" under [lsp] for the previous behaviour.
  • Faster runs. File discovery walks the tree once, in parallel, and no longer reads gitignored directories; paths that fail to analyze are listed in path order. The default report, --report-ignored, and the stale ignore comment report share one read of each file. File arguments are analyzed in parallel, and --fix analyzes again only the files it wrote. The analysis cache keeps the entries of other targets unparsed, rewrites its file only when this run's results changed, and holds at most 32 MiB of entries. On macOS, Windows, and 64-bit Linux, complexipy allocates with mimalloc.
  • Refactor plans are measured on their own function instead of the whole file, so --suggest-refactors grows linearly with the file size (#274). --failed, --fix, and --dry-run build plans only for functions over the limit, unless an output lists the others. The web demo builds no plans.
  • --diff and --staged read every file at the ref through one git cat-file --batch process, and look each file up at its own repository path. A file that moved since the ref is reported as new, and a run from a subdirectory finds the history of each file.
  • The language server analyzes on its own thread, so requests are answered while other documents are analyzed. Each document has its own debounce, and $/cancelRequest cancels a request that is still waiting.
  • The Python API releases the GIL while it analyzes and while compute_diff runs. functions, line_complexities, and refactor_plans return a new list over objects built once, instead of copying the data on every access.
  • A bare complexipy run whose configuration file sets no paths, or an empty list, stops with the missing paths error instead of analyzing nothing and passing. Set paths in the file or name the paths on the command line.
  • paths, output, and cache-dir read from a configuration file must stay inside the directory complexipy runs from, symbolic links included, or the run stops with an error that names the key. The same values on the command line are not restricted, so pass a path outside the project there. A diff reference that starts with -, from --diff, --diff-only, or the [diff] branch, also stops the run.
  • complexipy reads the first configuration file that parses and has valid values, and never merges files. The language server now moves on to the next file when one has an invalid value, as the CLI does. When a higher-priority file shadows a lower one that also holds settings, every run prints a warning that names the file not applied, so a project with both complexipy.toml and a [tool.complexipy] section in pyproject.toml sees it until it keeps its settings in one file. A configuration file that is not a regular file, that is larger than 4 MiB, or that is a symbolic link resolving outside its directory is skipped with a warning. A configuration error names the file and the line and column, or the key, instead of quoting the file.
  • A configuration file that sets a [diff] branch, [diff] staged = true, or snapshot-create = true prints a warning on stderr on every run the setting applies to, even under --quiet. The warning names the file and says how the setting changes the exit code. Pin the gate in CI with the matching flag, --isolated, or --config <path>, and create a snapshot with --snapshot-create on the command line instead of in the file.
  • Every function a module defines is scored on its own: a def under a module-level if, try, with, for, while, or match, and a method of a nested class, named Outer::Inner::method. These functions appear in every output and the gate checks them, so a run that passed before can fail on one, and a file's total can change. A function defined inside another function still counts toward the outer one.
  • An ignore marker counts only inside a comment: on the def line, on a line of its signature or decorators, or on its own line directly above. The same text in a string, a docstring, or a decorator argument, or in a trailing comment on the code line above, no longer suppresses the function. The marker words must be whole and separated by spaces or tabs only, so # complexipy: ignored is not a marker. Move such a marker into a comment on the def line.
  • A source file with a PEP 263 coding cookie is read in that encoding: UTF-8 and Latin-1 always, and an ASCII-compatible encoding such as cp1252 when the file is pure ASCII, so a Latin-1 file with non-ASCII bytes, which failed before, is now analyzed. A file that declares any other encoding, such as utf-7, or that declares an ASCII-compatible encoding and holds non-ASCII bytes, is reported as failed, and file_complexity() raises ValueError for it.
  • Functions of one file that share a name, such as a property's getter and setter, get separate entries in the snapshot, in --diff, and in compute_diff(): the first in source order keeps the name, and the next ones are keyed name#2, name#3. A snapshot written before this change can fail on such a file; run --snapshot-create once to rewrite it.
  • File discovery selects a *.py symbolic link only when it resolves to a regular file inside the analyzed directory. A link that leaves it, a dangling link, a device, a FIFO, a directory named *.py, and a directory that cannot be read are skipped, with a warning on stderr unless --quiet is set. A file whose name is not valid UTF-8 is reported as failed instead of skipped silently. A run that selects no file prints a warning even under --quiet, and --report-ignored also lists the *.py files that .gitignore, .ignore, and hidden-path rules skip.
  • A source file larger than 64 MiB is reported as failed instead of read, and file_complexity() raises ValueError for it and for a path that is not a regular file, such as a device. A snapshot that is not a regular file of at most 64 MiB inside its own directory stops the run with an error, and a cache file like that is ignored. The default cache is not used when .complexipy_cache resolves outside the directory complexipy runs from.
  • --fix rewrites only regular files inside the directory complexipy runs from. It skips a symbolic link, a file outside that directory, and a file that changed on disk after complexipy read it, and says so on stderr. It writes a new file next to the original and renames it into place, keeping the permission bits and the group but not setuid, setgid, extended attributes, or ACLs. Result files, the snapshot, and the cache are written the same way, so a symbolic link at an output path is replaced by a regular file instead of written through. --fix --dry-run writes nothing, not even the cache or the snapshot.
  • Text that comes from the analyzed files or the configuration, such as a path, a function name, a source line, or a configuration value, prints with its control characters and bidirectional formatting characters escaped: an escape character shows as \u{1b} and a line break as \u{a}. Tabs print as they are. This covers the report, --plain, the --fix diff, the warnings, and the language server log.
  • CSV output writes a cell that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab, or a carriage return with a leading ', so a spreadsheet shows it as text.
  • When the configuration has a problem, such as an unknown rule id or a shadowed configuration file, the language server shows the editor one fixed warning that points to the complexipy output log, and writes the details only to that log.
  • The VS Code extension runs in Restricted Mode instead of staying disabled there. In Restricted Mode it ignores a complexipy.server.path from workspace settings and runs the path from your user settings, or complexipy from the PATH, and trusting the workspace restarts the server with the workspace value. A relative complexipy.server.path resolves against the first workspace folder, where the server now starts, and relative PATH entries are skipped.
  • Boolean operators add one per sequence of like operators, as the cognitive complexity paper specifies. A boolean group nested in another one was compared with every sibling of its parent, so an expression that mixes operators across groups scored too high: (a or b) and (c and d) now scores 2 instead of 4, and not a and (b or c) scores 2 instead of 3. On a 1,915-function corpus, 4 scores changed, each down by 1.
  • GitLab Code Quality fingerprints no longer hash the function's line number, so a line added above a function keeps the fingerprint of every finding below it. A fingerprint now hashes the check, the path, the function name, and the finding's rank among the findings that share them. Every existing fingerprint changes once with this release, so the first comparison with a report from an earlier release shows every finding as new and every earlier one as fixed.
  • SARIF reports percent-encode artifactLocation.uri, so a path with spaces, quotes, non-ASCII characters, #, ?, or % points at the right file. $schema names the published OASIS SARIF 2.1.0 schema instead of a URL that returned 404. Each result carries partialFingerprints, which stay the same when lines are added above the finding, so uploads through a code scanning API do not duplicate alerts.
  • --quiet --ignore-complexity exits 0, like --ignore-complexity alone; it exited 1 when a function was over the limit. When stdout closes early, as in complexipy . | head, the output stops and the run keeps its exit code, instead of panicking with exit code 101 from the binary or 1 from the console script. The language server answers a message that is not valid JSON or JSON-RPC with an error response and keeps running, instead of exiting with 1.
  • An exclude pattern matches a path relative to each path argument, as before, and also relative to the working directory, so the CLI and the language server exclude the same files. With paths = ["src", "legacy"] and exclude = ["legacy/**"], they used to exclude opposite files. A CLI run whose path argument differs from the working directory can exclude more files than before, and never fewer. The server also matches each pattern relative to each paths entry, resolves .. in document paths before matching, and gives a nested workspace folder without a configuration file the configuration of the nearest enclosing folder that has one. A pattern that starts with /, ./, or ../, or ends with /, never matches, and the CLI and the server now warn about it. A file named on the command line is still analyzed when a pattern matches it, as in ruff. A --force-exclude flag that also excludes those files is tracked in #293.
  • C002 offers a loop guard replacement only when the nested if chain is the last statement of the loop body and each if the last statement of its parent. When statements follow the chain, the plan carries help text instead, because a continue guard would skip them: --fix used to write that guard, which could turn a while loop whose counter followed the chain into an infinite loop. C007 moves a single comment on the merged if lines, such as # type: ignore, to the merged line, and gives help text when those lines carry two or more comments or the inner if has its body on its header line.
  • --report-ignored, complexipy-ignored.json, and the stale ignore comment report show a file inside the working directory at the same path as the results. They used to show paths relative to the parent of each analyzed directory, or to a file argument's own directory, so complexipy . prefixed every path with the working directory's name. Each result's file_name now matches its path, also for a file reached through a symlink.
  • An internal error in the Python API raises ValueError from the analysis, diff, and ignore collection functions, and RuntimeError from run_cli and run_lsp, instead of pyo3_runtime.PanicException, which derives from BaseException. except Exception now catches it, so one file that hits an internal error no longer aborts a batch. The stubs and docs now name the errors each function raises.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• --diff and --staged read a path at the ref only when it was a regular file there. A path that was a symbolic link at the ref and is now a regular file compares as added instead of against the link's target text, so its functions above the threshold fail the gate. --staged also compares a staged change between a symbolic link and a regular file, which it skipped.
  • --staged reads a staged file whose name starts like a stage number, such as 0:a.py, instead of reading the staged a.py in its place.
  • branch = "" in the [diff] section turns the diff off, and the section's staged value with it, as documented, so the run checks every function against the threshold. Before, it compared against the index instead, so the exit code checked only the functions that changed.
  • --diff and compute_diff() read no old version of a path whose name holds a control character, so its functions report NEW. A name that ended in a carriage return read the old version of the same name without it.
  • A lone CR (\r) and CRLF now end a line everywhere, as they do for the tokenizer and in LSP 3.17. A file with CR line endings no longer panics while refactor plans are built or while the caret under a suggestion is drawn, reports every function on line 1, lets one ignore comment suppress the whole file, or takes quadratic time and output. --fix keeps a file's CR line endings, and the column of the caret under a suggestion counts characters, not bytes.
  • A long chained expression, such as a + a + ... + a, a.b.b..., f()()..., or a[0][0]..., no longer overflows the stack, which aborted the CLI and the language server and crashed the Python interpreter. A 300,000-term chain now analyzes in the CLI, the Python API, the language server, and the web demo.
  • Scoring a long boolean expression that mixes operators, and building refactor plans for a deep if chain, no longer take quadratic time.
  • --fix keeps what the rewritten code does. An else written as else :, or one after a condition that holds a run of quotes, is no longer missed. a or(b) and not a or(b) are parenthesized and inverted correctly. Each line keeps its own indentation, so a file that mixes tabs and spaces stays valid, and a tab-indented file gets tab-indented replacements. An inner if with its body on its header line no longer loses that body, C002 no longer rewrites a chain inside a nested function, and a # inside a string no longer hides a later multi-line string from the check that refuses the rewrite.
  • A file reached through several path arguments, such as complexipy . src src/a.py, or through a symlink next to it, is analyzed, reported, and fixed once.
  • --report-ignored lists each suppressed location as path:line # comment, followed by the count, as its help text and the docs describe. It used to print only the count.
  • Suggestion snippets honor --color no, NO_COLOR, and piped output, and a comment in a snippet no longer colors every line after it. Color is decided on each run, so a Python host that calls run_cli several times follows each run's terminal and NO_COLOR.
  • A --diff ref wider than the terminal no longer panics while the banner is drawn.
  • compute_diff(current, "origin/main") works as documented: invocation_path defaults to None. Ctrl-C stops the console script at once instead of after the run finishes. A process forked after a parallel call no longer hangs on its next parallel call. The stubs and docs drop the nonexistent DiffEntry.delta, fix an exclude example that matched nothing, and show the real snapshot entry format.
  • The language server reads each frame as it arrives, up to 256 MiB, so a huge Content-Length no longer makes it allocate that size or abort, and a broken frame is reported on stderr before the server stops. A request after shutdown, or one whose id is neither an integer nor a string, gets an InvalidRequest error instead of no answer. After a failed handshake the server exits instead of waiting for stdin to close. file://localhost/... resolves to the local path, and a URI with a remote host resolves to a UNC path on Windows and to no path elsewhere, so the server reads the right configuration. Hover shows a function name such as Box::__init__ literally instead of rendering it as Markdown.
  • The VS Code extension stops a server that does not start within 30 seconds and shows an error, so a later restart is no longer blocked. It keeps one output channel instead of adding one per restart.
  • The web demo loads a fresh analyzer after an analysis crashes, instead of failing every later analysis until the page reloads.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• complexipy now treats the content of the analyzed repository as untrusted. This release fixes the issues described in GHSA-8p2q-4h62-q593, GHSA-9qgh-5xjp-8g3m, GHSA-wg3w-cmfg-c94w, GHSA-mh97-m2f8-q8vj, and, for the VS Code extension 0.4.0, GHSA-wpx6-54p3-527q. Upgrading is recommended for every user.

See the release notes for the full details.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• A language server: complexipy lsp speaks the Language Server Protocol on stdio, so any editor with an LSP client gets complexity feedback with no per-editor code. It answers inlay hint requests with the cognitive complexity of each function and, optionally, the increment contributed by each line; it answers hover requests with the function total, its threshold status, and the top refactoring suggestion, built on demand for the hovered function so large files stay responsive; and it publishes a warning for every function above max-complexity-allowed. Diagnostics respect inline ignore comments, so the editor and the CLI agree. The per-function hint sits at the end of the line that closes the declaration, so a wrapped signature keeps the hint on its closing line, and a document that does not parse keeps the last parsed hints plus one complexipy-parse-error warning, placed where the parser fails, until it parses again. Configuration problems, such as an unknown rule id in select, appear in the editor as a warning message (#272). The server reloads the configuration when a configuration file at a folder root changes, in editors that watch files for it (#257). A Zed extension in zed/ starts the server in Zed, and the inlay hints carry a left padding so they do not touch the code (#255). See Editor Integration for the VS Code, Neovim, and Zed setup.

  • The VS Code extension is now a client of the language server and drops its bundled WASM engine (#253). Results update while you type, with no save (#133), and hints and warnings follow max-complexity-allowed and the [tool.complexipy.lsp] settings (#127). The extension needs the complexipy command, and a complexipy.server.path setting points it at a specific binary.

  • The VS Code extension is published to OpenVSX as well as the Visual Studio Marketplace, so VSCodium and other VS Code forks can install it (#145). A vscode-v* tag publishes the same VSIX to both registries.

  • A [tool.complexipy.lsp] configuration section, with inlay-hints (threshold, always, or never), per-line-hints, and diagnostics. Hints are gated on max-complexity-allowed by default, so a project that sets no options sees feedback only where it matters.

  • complexipy-core gains a config feature that owns configuration file discovery, so the CLI and the server read complexipy.toml, .complexipy.toml, and pyproject.toml through one code path.

  • The server applies exclude one pattern at a time: a malformed pattern is reported once per configuration load and skipped while the remaining patterns keep applying, and a list too large to compile as one program is reported once and still applied. A CLI run stops on either.

  • Each workspace folder reads its own configuration (#273). In a workspace with several folders, a document uses the threshold, rule selection, exclude patterns, and [tool.complexipy.lsp] settings of the deepest folder that contains it, and a document outside every folder uses the first folder. The server declares workspace folder support, so folders that the editor adds or removes take effect without a restart.

  • Per-rule suppression and rule selection (#208). --select and --ignore (repeatable and comma-separated) pick the active refactoring rules, and ignore wins on conflict. complexipy.toml, .complexipy.toml, and pyproject.toml take matching select and ignore keys, and a flag replaces the toml key it names. A toml value splits on commas like the flags, so select = "C007, C002" names two rules. An ignore comment accepts a bracketed rule list, # complexipy: ignore[C007], which suppresses only the named rules for one function, while a bare marker keeps suppressing the whole function. An inactive rule disappears from every output format and never consumes a slot of the per-function plan cap, so a hidden rule can never block a visible one. An unknown rule id warns on stderr that it matches no registered rule, and a second warning says so when select and ignore leave no rule active. Rule selection never changes the exit code.

  • --fix applies machine-applicable suggestions to the source files (#204). A suggestion is fixable when its tier is MachineApplicable and its replacement is a faithful splice (spliceable), which covers C002 (loop guards) and C007 (collapsible if); C005 is not spliceable and stays out. --fix changes only functions whose complexity is above max-complexity-allowed, and every pass checks the threshold again, so a function stops changing once it passes. Functions at or under the threshold keep their suggestions in the report and are never rewritten. One run fixes every analyzed file, bottom-to-top within each file, and prints a syntax-highlighted unified diff of the applied changes, with line numbers, one context line per hunk, and the rule that fired, plus a summary of fixed and skipped fixes that shows the reduction per fix. Every summary line carries the file's line numbers from before the run, and each skip reports once. The run repeats pass by pass, up to 8 passes, until no fixable plan remains, so a fix that exposes a new fixable plan is applied in a later pass; later passes label their diffs. Long diff rows truncate at the terminal width. When nothing is fixable the run prints No fixes to apply. --fix runs in any git state: uncommitted changes, untracked files, and a missing repository never block it, and no extra flag is needed. A fix keeps the file's line endings and its trailing newline. A fix that would produce invalid Python is reverted and reported, and the write is a parse-checked temp file renamed over the original with its permissions kept. The report and the gates measure the post-fix state, so re-analyzing a fixed file shows the finding gone and the exact measured reduction. --fix --dry-run prints only the diff and writes nothing. --select/--ignore decide which rules may fix.

  • Python 3.15 support (#265). Lazy imports (PEP 810) and unpacking in comprehensions (PEP 798) now parse in the CLI, the language server, the Python API, and the web build. A lazy import adds no complexity, and an unpacking comprehension scores like the plain one. Releases now publish CPython 3.15 wheels for Windows and macOS.

  • A JSON schema for the configuration (#270). complexipy.schema.json describes every key of complexipy.toml, .complexipy.toml, and [tool.complexipy], including [diff] and [lsp], so a TOML language server such as Taplo offers completion, hover text, and validation. The schema rejects unknown keys. complexipy itself still ignores them.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• lsp is a reserved first argument: complexipy lsp starts the language server, so a file or directory with that name needs complexipy -- lsp to be analyzed. On a terminal the server prints that hint when both the reserved word and a path named lsp are present.
  • StringOrList moved from complexipy-cli::types to the new complexipy-core config module, and the CLI still re-exports it from its old path. Every workspace crate remains publish = false, so no published Rust API changes.
  • Added manylinux_2_31_riscv64 wheel builds for RISC-V support. The release matrix now separates the Rust toolchain triple (target) from the platform shorthand (arch), which keeps the existing wheel and artifact names unchanged. (#259)
  • RuleCategory, Applicability, and DiffStatus are real enum.Enum subclasses: they iterate, they carry .name and .value, and isinstance(x, enum.Enum) holds.
  • requires-python is now >=3.8,<3.16, so installers stop choosing complexipy on a Python version no release has built or tested. The bound rises when a release adds the next Python version. On Python 3.16 and later, pip falls back to 8.0.1, the last release without the bound. (#281)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• --color governs every styled line the CLI writes, on stdout and stderr. auto turns color off when the stream is not a terminal or NO_COLOR is set, no removes it from the report, the banner, and the warnings, and --plain output is never styled. In 8.0.1 the report carried ANSI codes on a pipe, under --color no, and under NO_COLOR.

See the release notes for the full details.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Docs, package metadata, and embedded links (rule doc URLs in --suggest-refactors output, SARIF report URIs) now point to the complexipy.com custom domain instead of the GitHub Pages default. (#252)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The sdist now includes the LICENSE file, which was previously missing from the published source distribution.

See the release notes for the full details.

Migration

See the migration guide for the breaking changes below.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The Python CLI is retired: complexipy is now a native Rust implementation exposed through a thin console-script shim, so the whole pipeline runs without a Python interpreter. The Python API is unchanged and now includes the diff comparison (compute_diff, has_regressions, DiffEntry, DiffStatus) backed by the same Rust engine as the CLI. The extension module keeps being distributed via maturin wheels. (#224, #243)

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Git-URL analysis (complexipy <repository-url>) - local paths only.
  • Legacy cache migration - the previous .complexipy_cache/<hash>.json layout is no longer migrated; existing legacy files are ignored and the delta history starts fresh.
  • Legacy snapshot files - snapshots created with older versions are no longer detected; recreate them with --snapshot-create.
  • -mx short flag for --max-complexity-allowed - carried over from the Python CLI but never ported to the clap-based parser; use --max-complexity-allowed instead.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The C007 collapsible-if rule no longer suggests merging a nested if when a same-level statement with side effects precedes it - the merge would change program behavior. Comments in multiline headers and trailing comments are handled instead of being misplaceable by the replacement. (#228, #236)
  • The C007 preceding-statement guard no longer fails when blank or comment-only lines sit between the outer and inner if: the indent step detection now skips such lines, so the merge is still rejected instead of producing a replacement that drops code. (#245)
  • The C002 loop-guards suggestion keeps statements that sit between the chained ifs: they now appear in the replacement between the corresponding guards instead of being dropped. Guard conditions are now parenthesized (if not (<cond>):), so inverting conditions with and or or no longer silently changes what the guard skips.
  • The C005 extract-predicate suggestion keeps the statement keyword: while conditions stay while loops, and elif conditions get help text only instead of a broken standalone if replacement. The predicate body indent now follows the file's indent step.
  • C002 and C007 refuse machine suggestions when the shifted body holds a multi-line string literal: dedenting would change the string's value. The plans carry help text instead.
  • C002 loop guards strip a redundant top-level not from the guard condition (if not a: becomes guard if a:), and C005 predicate names get an underscore suffix when the source already defines the generated name.
  • C005 extract-predicate now emits a module-level helper whose parameters are the condition's free variables (attribute bases included, builtins excluded), so the helper is unit-testable. The snippet shows the enclosing context at the statement's real indentation. Conditions that bind a name (:=) or contain a lambda/comprehension get help text only.

See the release notes for the full details.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The release pipeline now retries artifact uploads with pinned workflow versions and only notifies downstream repositories on tag releases, keeping non-tag pushes silent.
  • Pinned maturin version in the release workflow to avoid GitHub API rate limits when resolving the latest version inside Docker build containers.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Snapshot entries for analyzed files are updated in place instead of being moved to the end of the file: partial runs (e.g. pre-commit hooks analyzing only staged files) no longer reorder the snapshot, so the snapshot stays byte-identical across commits that do not change complexity. (#226)

See the release notes for the full details.

Migration

The deprecated --output-json, --output-csv, --output-gitlab, --output-sarif, and --ratchet flags and their TOML keys were removed; use --output-format and --diff instead. See the migration guide for each removed flag and key with its replacement.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• --suggest-refactors is now a clippy-style lint system: stable rule IDs (C001-C005, C007, C011), category and applicability metadata, path:line:col anchors with caret spans, verbatim suggestion rendering, and a documentation link per rule. (#209)
  • Refactor-plan findings are included in JSON, SARIF, and GitLab exports when --suggest-refactors is passed; the SARIF rule catalog is built dynamically from the plans encountered. (#209)
  • compute_diff, has_regressions, DiffEntry, and DiffStatus are now part of the public Python API, so CI tools can consume diff results as objects instead of parsing terminal output; DiffStatus provides named constants such as DiffStatus.REGRESSED. (#210)
  • collect_removable_ignored_locations() and RemovableIgnore are exported from the Python API. Every run now reports ignore comments that are no longer necessary (path:line function=X complexity=N <comment>) when the suppressed function is back under the allowed limit - the exit code is unaffected, the report is suppressed under --quiet, and it works under --plain. (#213)
  • --staged flag for git-index comparison - answers "what complexity am I about to commit?" instead of only what changed in the working tree; --staged alone defaults the baseline to HEAD and enforces, while --diff <ref> --staged enforces against the ref. (#218)
  • [tool.complexipy.diff] TOML section so the comparison policy lives in the repository config: branch = "main" makes a plain complexipy . run behave like --diff main (enforcement included), staged = true enables staged comparison by default, and branch = "" opts out. CLI flags take precedence over the section. (#219)
  • Refactor reductions are now measured instead of estimated: for every machine-applicable suggestion (C002, C007) the replacement is spliced into the source, re-parsed, and re-scored, so estimated_reduction and estimated_complexity_after report the literal delta of applying the suggestion - and ranking, overlap resolution, and the noise filter all operate on measured values. The new reduction_is_measured flag on RefactorPlan separates measured plans from help-only formula estimates, which the CLI renders with a ~ qualifier (Estimated reduction: ~-2) while measured plans render plain (Reduction: -2). Guard suggestions are now faithful splices for loops with statements before or after the if-chain and for multi-line loop headers; measurement failures fall back to the formula estimate - never a panic, never a fabricated number. (#225)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Refactor-plan reduction estimates are now honest: the reduction math was rewritten and validated against measured before/after complexity, C004 no longer suggests splitting match statements, C006 was deleted because its gate could never fire, and C011 now fires on try → with → try chains. Overlapping plans are deduped against every overlap and capped at 5, reporting dropped ones as "... and N more suggestions". (#209)
  • Condition extraction in the refactor rules now tracks bracket depth, string literals, and walrus := instead of a naive rfind(':'). (#209)
  • file_complexity() now returns cwd-relative paths (matching git diff --name-only), and nested invocations resolve git paths via a git ls-files basename lookup - without this, diffing per-file results silently marked every function as NEW. (#210)
  • Community standards files were added: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, issue templates, and a pull request template. (#201)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Snapshot updates now merge with the existing snapshot instead of replacing it: only the files analyzed in a run are touched, so partial runs (e.g. pre-commit hooks analyzing only staged files) no longer erase the baseline for unanalyzed files. (#215)
  • The docs footer now renders its links as styled links instead of raw markdown text, on both the English and Spanish landing pages. (#216)

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• RefactorPlan.steps - replaced by the concrete suggestion / help fields on the plan. (#209)
  • CodeSnippet from the public API; CodeSuggestion is exported in its place. (#209)
  • --output-json / -j, --output-csv / -c, --output-gitlab, and --output-sarif / -sr - use --output-format instead. (#221)
  • --ratchet / -R - --diff enforces the threshold by default. (#221)
  • TOML keys output-json, output-csv, output-gitlab, output-sarif, flat staged, flat ratchet, and the undocumented details = "low" alias. (#221)

These removals land in 7.0.0. See the migration guide for each removed flag and key with its replacement.

See the release notes for the full details.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • --exclude and --output-format now accept comma-separated values (--exclude tests/**,src/**), avoiding shell expansion issues. (#199)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Output now shows the correct relative path from the current working directory when analyzing a single file or a directory. (#198)
  • --output-sarif help text now carries a deprecation notice, clarifying that SARIF output is moving to a different mechanism. (#199)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Decomposed the monolithic 316-line main() function into a clean orchestrator (~80 lines) with extracted business logic in domain-specific utils/ modules (config.py, paths.py, ignored.py). (#199)
  • Introduced RunConfig, ExitReport, and SnapshotEvaluation dataclasses, replacing mutable accumulators and positional tuple unpacking. (#199)
  • Eliminated all global console declarations - the console instance is constructed once and passed explicitly. (#199)
  • Refactored get_arguments_value from a 20-parameter function returning a 15-element tuple to a dict-based approach. (#199)
  • Added 30 new tests covering config resolution and snapshot evaluation logic. (#199)

See the release notes for the full details.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Fixed git path resolution when running --diff from a nested subdirectory inside a repository, which previously caused "not a git repository" errors. (#196)
  • Fixed ruff lint configuration to use a glob pattern instead of a directory exclusion for test files. (#196)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Simplified the diff CLI - --diff now always enforces --max-complexity-allowed, while --diff-only provides the visual-only comparison. --ratchet is deprecated in favour of this model. (#196)
  • Integrated diff output into the main analysis flow instead of producing it as a separate post-processing step. (#196)
  • Removed the redundant "Failed functions" output section - failed functions are now shown inline in the per-file summary. (#196)
  • Added AGENTS.md for AI agent context.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:

  • except handlers now charge 1 + nesting_level instead of a flat +1. (#192)
  • with blocks no longer incorrectly raise the nesting level. (#192)
  • Direct recursion now emits +1 for each self-call via a scope-aware RecursionFinder, correctly skipping nested function/class definitions and lambdas. (#192)
  • Lambda expressions are now included in boolean-op counting, recursing into the body at nesting_level + 1. (#192)
  • Comprehensions (ListComp, SetComp, DictComp, Generator) now charge 1 + nesting_level per generator and +1 per if filter. (#192)
  • Nested ternaries now recurse at nesting_level + 1, so inner ternaries receive the correct nesting increment. (#192)
  • for/while else clauses are now collected at the loop's own nesting level, not +1. (#192)
  • Bare expression statements now count boolean ops (e.g. foo(a and b)). (#192)
  • The for iterable now counts boolean ops, for parity with while. (#192)

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
Use the official action:

- uses: rohaquinlop/complexipy-action@v9
  with:
      paths: src tests
      max_complexity_allowed: 15
      output_json: true

Or run directly:

- name: Check complexity
  run: |
      pip install complexipy
      complexipy . --max-complexity-allowed 15

docs.title: GitHub Code Scanning (SARIF)
docs.text:
Upload complexity violations as inline PR annotations using SARIF:

- name: Run complexipy
  run: complexipy . --output-format sarif --output complexipy-results.sarif --ignore-complexity

- name: Upload SARIF results
  uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with:
      sarif_file: complexipy-results.sarif

docs.title: Pre-commit Hook
docs.text:
Add to .pre-commit-config.yaml:

repos:
    - repo: https://github.com/rohaquinlop/complexipy-pre-commit
      rev: v9.0.0
      hooks:
          - id: complexipy
            args: [--max-complexity-allowed=15]

pre-commit passes each changed file as an argument, and exclude does not apply to explicit file arguments unless --force-exclude is set. Add --force-exclude to args for the configured exclude to apply.

docs.title: GitLab CI
docs.text:
.complexipy_code_quality:
    image: python:3.11
    script:
        - pip install complexipy
        - complexipy . --output-format gitlab --output complexipy-code-quality.json --ignore-complexity --max-complexity-allowed 15
    artifacts:
        when: always
        reports:
            codequality: complexipy-code-quality.json

complexity:
    extends: .complexipy_code_quality
    rules:
        - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
        - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

Use --ignore-complexity when your main goal is to upload the report even if violations exist. GitLab will still display the findings in the merge request widget and pipeline UI.

If you also want the job to fail when the threshold is exceeded, split the workflow into two jobs:

complexity_check:
    image: python:3.11
    script:
        - pip install complexipy
        - complexipy . --max-complexity-allowed 15

complexity_report:
    image: python:3.11
    script:
        - pip install complexipy
        - complexipy . --output-format gitlab --output complexipy-code-quality.json --ignore-complexity --max-complexity-allowed 15
    artifacts:
        when: always
        reports:
            codequality: complexipy-code-quality.json

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text:
Flag Description Default --exclude Exclude glob patterns relative to each provided path. Use patterns like tests/** for directories or src/legacy/file.py for specific files. --select <ids> Report only the named refactoring rules or rule groups, e.g. --select C001,C007 or --select complexity. Repeatable and comma-separated all rules --ignore <ids> Never report the named refactoring rules or rule groups, e.g. --ignore C007 or --ignore readability. Wins over --select. Repeatable and comma-separated --max-complexity-allowed Complexity threshold 15 --snapshot-create Save the current violations above the threshold into complexipy-snapshot.json false --snapshot-ignore Skip comparing against the snapshot even if it exists false --failed Show only functions above the complexity threshold false --suggest-refactors Show deterministic Rust AST-based refactor plans in rich CLI output. With --plain, adds one line per plan false --fix Apply every fixable suggestion (Safe to apply and spliceable) of the functions above max-complexity-allowed to the source files, then report the post-fix state (see Applying Fixable Suggestions). Implies --suggest-refactors false --dry-run Print only the unified diff of the fixes that --fix would apply, and write nothing. Implies --fix false --color <auto\|yes\|no> Use color auto --sort <asc\|desc\|file_name> Sort results asc --quiet Suppress output false --ignore-complexity Don't exit with error on threshold breach false --version Show installed complexipy version and exit - --top <n> Show only the n most complex functions, globally sorted by complexity descending - --plain Emit plain text lines as <path>:<line> <function> <complexity>. Cannot be combined with --quiet false --output-format <format> Select a machine-readable output format. Repeat the flag to request multiple formats (json, csv, gitlab, sarif) - --output <path> Write machine-readable output to a file or directory. Use a directory when emitting multiple formats. Use - to write a single format to stdout: the console output is suppressed as with --quiet, and warnings and errors go to stderr - --cache-dir <path> Store the per-function cache in this directory instead of .complexipy_cache/ (see Cache Configuration) .complexipy_cache --diff <ref> Show a complexity diff against a git reference and enforce the threshold. Fails on regressions above --max-complexity-allowed (see Complexity Diff) - --diff-only <ref> Show a complexity diff visually without affecting the exit code (see Complexity Diff) - --staged Compare staged (git index) changes against the --diff ref (default HEAD). Answers "what complexity am I about to commit?" (see Complexity Diff) false --check-script Report module-level (script) complexity as a synthetic <module> entry false --no-ignore Analyze every function, disregarding inline ignore comments (# complexipy: ignore, # noqa: complexipy) false --report-ignored List every file:line where an ignore comment suppresses a function. --quiet hides the list false --force-exclude Apply exclude to files passed explicitly as arguments, such as the file names pre-commit passes false --isolated Ignore every configuration file. Cannot be combined with --config false --config <path> Read the configuration from this file only, instead of the invocation directory's files - --explain <rule> Print a refactoring rule's id, name, category, applicability, description, and documentation link, then exit without analyzing anything. An unknown id exits with an error that lists the valid ids -

Boolean flags take an explicit value only in the attached form --flag=<true|false>. A bare flag means true, and the following argument is never consumed as its value.

Example:

# Exclude a directory recursively under the provided root
complexipy . --exclude "tests/**"
# Exclude a specific file
complexipy . --exclude "src/legacy/old_code.py"

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Both Ruff and complexipy help improve Python code quality, but they measure different aspects of complexity and serve complementary purposes. Ruff's PLR0912 measures structural complexity, testing, and branch density, while complexipy measures how difficult code is for humans to understand and maintain.

docs.title: Ruff's PLR0912: Too Many Branches
docs.text: Ruff's PLR0912 (too-many-branches) rule is based on cyclomatic complexity and counts the number of decision points in a function.

docs.title: How Ruff Counts Branches
docs.text:
Ruff counts each of these as a branch:

  • if, elif, else statements
  • for and while loops
  • except clauses, and the else and finally clauses of a try
  • Pattern matching cases

The default threshold is typically 12 branches per function.

docs.title: Example: Ruff Analysis
docs.text:
def example(a, b, c, d):
    if a:           # Branch 1
        return 1
    elif b:         # Branch 2
        return 2
    elif c:         # Branch 3
        return 3
    elif d:         # Branch 4
        return 4
    else:           # Branch 5
        return 0
# Ruff: 5 branches

docs.title: complexipy: Cognitive Complexity
docs.text: complexipy implements cognitive complexity, which weights branches by their nesting level to reflect human understanding.

docs.title: How complexipy Scores
docs.text:
complexipy uses the formula: complexity = base_score + nesting_level

def example(a, b, c, d):
    if a:           # +1 (1 + 0 nesting)
        return 1
    elif b:         # +1 (elif counts as +1)
        return 2
    elif c:         # +1
        return 3
    elif d:         # +1
        return 4
    else:           # +1 (no nesting increment)
        return 0
# complexipy: 5 points

docs.title: 1. Nesting is Critical in complexipy
docs.text:
Ruff treats all branches equally:

# Ruff: 3 branches
def flat_logic(a, b, c):
    if a:           # Branch 1
        return 1
    if b:           # Branch 2
        return 2
    if c:           # Branch 3
        return 3

# Ruff: 3 branches (same as above)
def nested_logic(a, b, c):
    if a:           # Branch 1
        if b:       # Branch 2
            if c:   # Branch 3
                return 1

complexipy accounts for nesting:

# complexipy: 3 points
def flat_logic(a, b, c):
    if a:           # +1
        return 1
    if b:           # +1
        return 2
    if c:           # +1
        return 3

# complexipy: 6 points (much worse!)
def nested_logic(a, b, c):
    if a:           # +1 (1 + 0)
        if b:       # +2 (1 + 1)
            if c:   # +3 (1 + 2)
                return 1

docs.title: 2. else Clauses
docs.text:
Ruff: Counts else as a branch (+1)

complexipy: else adds +1 too, but never a nesting increment, however deep it sits

# Ruff: 2 branches
# complexipy: 2 points
def check(value):
    if value > 0:   # Ruff: +1, complexipy: +1
        return "positive"
    else:           # Ruff: +1, complexipy: +1
        return "non-positive"

docs.title: 3. Boolean Operators
docs.text:
Only complexipy counts boolean operators:

Ruff: Does not count and/or; the if is the only branch

complexipy: Counts each sequence of like operators once, read left to right; a change between and and or starts a new sequence

# Ruff: 1 branch (the if)
# complexipy: 3 points (1 for if, +2 for boolean ops)
def check(a, b, c):
    if a and b or c:
        return True

docs.title: 4. Match Statements (Python 3.10+)
docs.text:
Ruff: Counts each case as a branch

complexipy: match adds +1 once for all its cases, and the content of each case is nested

# Ruff: 4 branches (2 cases + 2 nested ifs)
# complexipy: 5 points (match +1, each nested if +2)
match value:        # Ruff: +0, complexipy: +1
    case 1:         # Ruff: +1, complexipy: +0
        if x:       # Ruff: +1, complexipy: +2 (1 + nesting)
            pass
    case 2:         # Ruff: +1, complexipy: +0
        if y:       # Ruff: +1, complexipy: +2 (1 + nesting)
            pass

docs.title: Practical Comparison Example
docs.text:
Here's a real-world scenario showing how the two tools differ:

def process_payment(order):
    if order is None:                              # Ruff: 1, complexipy: 1
        return False

    if not order.is_valid():                       # Ruff: 2, complexipy: 2
        return False

    if order.payment_method == "credit_card":      # Ruff: 3, complexipy: 3
        if order.amount > 1000:                    # Ruff: 4, complexipy: 5 (1+1 nesting)
            if not verify_fraud_check(order):      # Ruff: 5, complexipy: 8 (1+2 nesting)
                return False
        return process_credit_card(order)
    elif order.payment_method == "paypal":         # Ruff: 6, complexipy: 9
        return process_paypal(order)
    else:                                           # Ruff: 7, complexipy: 10
        return False

# Final Scores:
# Ruff: 7 branches
# complexipy: 10 points

In this example:

  • Ruff counts 7 branches, under its default limit of 12
  • complexipy gives it 10 points, with most complexity coming from the nested fraud check
  • complexipy better identifies that the deeply nested fraud check is the problematic part

docs.title: Use Ruff (PLR0912) When:
docs.text:
• You need to measure structural complexity and branch density
  • You're designing test coverage strategies
  • You want to limit the absolute number of decision points
  • You're already using Ruff for other linting

docs.title: Use complexipy When:
docs.text:
• You want to identify code that's hard for humans to understand
  • You're focused on code readability and maintainability
  • Nesting and flow complexity are concerns in your codebase
  • You're conducting code reviews focused on comprehension

docs.title: Use Both! (Recommended)
docs.text:
Ruff and complexipy are complementary:

# In your pre-commit or CI pipeline
ruff check . --select=PLR0912  # Catch functions with too many branches
complexipy . --max-complexity-allowed 15  # Catch deeply nested code

Ruff catches wide functions (many branches), while complexipy catches deep functions (heavy nesting). Together, they provide comprehensive complexity coverage.

docs.title: Ruff Configuration
docs.text:
# pyproject.toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["PLR0912"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-branches = 12

docs.title: complexipy Configuration
docs.text:
# pyproject.toml
[tool.complexipy]
max-complexity-allowed = 15

docs.title: Using Both in CI
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/quality.yml
- name: Ruff Linting
  run: ruff check . --select=PLR0912

- name: Cognitive Complexity Check
  run: complexipy . --max-complexity-allowed 15

docs.title: Migration Strategy
docs.text:
If you're already using Ruff and want to add complexipy:

  1. Baseline First: Run complexipy . --snapshot-create to capture current state
  2. Set Thresholds: Start with a higher threshold (e.g., 20) and lower it over time
  3. Fix New Code: Only fail CI on new violations
  4. Gradual Improvement: Refactor legacy code opportunistically

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Feature Ruff PLR0912 complexipy Based on Cyclomatic Complexity Cognitive Complexity Counts nesting ❌ No ✅ Yes else penalty ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (+1, no nesting increment) Boolean operators ❌ No ✅ Yes match statements ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (+1 for the whole match) Best for Structural, testing, branch density How difficult code is to understand Threshold ~12 branches ~15 points Performance Fast (Rust) Very fast (Rust)

The Bottom Line: Ruff's PLR0912 measures structural complexity and branch density (useful for testing and analysis), while complexipy measures how difficult code is for humans to understand and maintain by penalizing nesting and flow breaks. Both are valuable, and using them together provides the best coverage for code quality.

docs.text:
